subject.title: Rescue: add watchdog core service and cron engine

question: Should OpenClaw core accept an internal `rescueWatchdog` cron payload that can restart managed gateway services and run non-interactive doctor repair, or should this remain outside core until a narrower approved rescue design lands?
rationale: The patch is not only a code repair: it creates an unattended recovery surface with command execution, service-control, and availability implications, so automation cannot decide the permanent product/security boundary.

options.title: Accept after rebase and proof
options.body: Require the branch to preserve current command cron jobs, add live redacted recovery proof, and get maintainer security/product approval before merge.

options.title: Defer to the canonical reliability issue
options.body: Keep the broader rescue direction tracked in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/36314 and close or split this branch if maintainers want a different architecture.

options.title: Narrow to daemon hardening only
options.body: Extract only the service/launchd hardening that is independently useful and leave the watchdog cron payload for a later sponsored PR.

recommendation.title: Accept after rebase and proof
recommendation.body: Require the branch to preserve current command cron jobs, add live redacted recovery proof, and get maintainer security/product approval before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The current cron command contract and relevant recent main history route through this owner, and the decision touches that same runtime boundary.
